item.title: Corridor Brief — Monday, 21 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Monday, 21 September 2026 — Trump-Xi summit set for September 24 in Washington as $14 billion Taiwan arms package, $1 trillion China trade surplus loom; Bessent calls China talks ‘very successful’ as Asian markets rally and oil eases on Hormuz reopening; Houthis fire ballistic missile at Riyadh in most intense Yemen-linked attack on Saudi capital since 2022 truce; Ukraine launches war's largest drone barrage on Moscow during final day of Russia's parliamentary election, hits oil refinery; Merz calls Mecklenburg-Vorpommern loss a ‘disaster’ as AfD narrowly wins state, Die Linke takes Berlin.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Sunday, 20 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Sunday, 20 September 2026 — Bessent and China's He Lifeng open trade talks ahead of the Trump-Xi summit; Anthropic pushes toward a $2 trillion IPO as its own alignment lead warns of unresolved AI extinction risk; Paramount could settle its $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery fight with states this weekend; IATA halves its 2026 airline profit forecast on the Gulf fuel shock; and Germany's Merz faces an AfD breakthrough test in two state elections.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Saturday, 19 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Saturday, 19 September 2026 — Houthi forces capture a Red Sea port and push a second Gulf oil corridor toward crisis as the Bank of Japan hikes to a 31-year high; Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after 56 years; the FCC clears Paramount to take $24 billion in Gulf financing for its Warner Bros. Discovery buyout; Anthropic's revenue run-rate tops $100 billion as researchers use Claude to breach OpenAI's systems; and Ottawa's Conservative caucus fractures just as Carney sets a ‘most consequential’ fall legislative agenda.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Friday, 18 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Friday, 18 September 2026 — the Federal Reserve delivers its first hike since 2023 under new Chair Kevin Warsh; Saudi Arabia's crippled East-West pipeline forces an emergency reroute of 5% of world oil supply as the IRGC strikes a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz; the Bank of Japan hikes to a 31-year high and the Bank of England holds on a hawkish 6-3 split; Washington strips Canadian goods from $280 billion in federal procurement the same week Carney pitches Canada as the EU's first associate member; the DOJ backs Paramount's bond fight in the $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery merger; and Anthropic discloses Claude now leads 26% of its own AI R&D.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Thursday, 17 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Thursday, 17 September 2026 — the Federal Reserve delivers its first rate hike since 2023 and pencils in no cuts through 2027 as Trump publicly attacks his own pick, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays offline with Brent above $107 and full repair six weeks out, US diesel hits an all-time record $6.31 a gallon, the ECB's own 25-point hike takes effect the same week, Carney's Canada Investment Summit closes with nearly $500 billion pledged and a cut to a 6.4% effective tax rate on new investment, the IAEA refers Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years, NATO downs a drone over Lithuania as a Russian frigate confronts a Danish helicopter, and OpenAI discloses new AI misalignment incidents while pursuing a $1.2 trillion valuation to avoid an IPO.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Wednesday, 16 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Wednesday, 16 September 2026 — the Fed decides today under Chair Kevin Warsh with markets pricing a first rate hike since 2023 as Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut a fifth day and Brent nears $110, Carney's Canada Investment Summit closes with nearly $500 billion pledged while the US trade track stays frozen, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind confirm weeks of closed-door AI-safety talks, Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington September 24 as a tariff truce on agriculture and energy takes shape, the IDF and Shin Bet confirm killing Hamas' Rafah Brigade commander, a Russian drone strikes a diplomatic train near the Polish border, and the Supreme Court gives states until September 25 to answer a bid to derail the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery antitrust suit.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Tuesday, 15 September 2026
item.description: Corridor Brief for Tuesday, 15 September 2026 — Saudi Arabia's pipeline shutdown and the Houthi seizure of Yemen's Mayyun Island leave the Gulf's oil routes without a working backup as Brent tops $107 and a strike near Hormuz's Hengam Island kills one, US diesel hits a record $6.05 a gallon and August CPI accelerates to 3.4% ahead of Wednesday's FOMC as the 10-year Treasury briefly tops 5%, Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt energy-target strikes as Kyiv and Moscow stop short of confirming it, Carney welcomes Trump's trade-deal comments while opening a three-day European tour and Canada's own inflation holds at 3.0%, SoftBank takes on an $11.87 billion loan to keep funding OpenAI as Anthropic's Amodei calls to “pace the frontier” on AI safety and Trump rejects any guardrails beyond a “strong, smart president,” and Paramount's $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery is ordered into antitrust settlement talks.

item.title: Corridor Brief — Monday, 14 September 2026

item.title: The Instrument That Outlived the Emergency: What Actually Survived 9/11
item.description: Twenty-five years on, the durable legacy is not the wars and not the airports. It is a routine administrative power to cut an institution out of the dollar system, created in 2001 and given a permanent office in 2004 — and an energy position that inverted over the same quarter century.
